results.quote: sc-compose and atm crates should be blocked from any production release crate.
results.context: Phase D planning session 2026-11-11
results.deterministic_check: Plan: inspect proposed normal/build dependencies. Development: inspect cargo metadata and cargo tree normal/build graphs for each published crate and supported feature set for sc-compose or agent-team-mail.

criteria.no: The item is exclusively a dev-only test/benchmark reference, external executable command/help change, or documentation without a production dependency policy, with no normal/build declaration or production graph change.
criteria.unclear: The work area cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: The item changes normal/build dependencies or resolved production graphs of published sc-runtime crates, or explicitly sets/preserves the production graph constraint excluding sc-compose and ATM crates. relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` change the area governed by `anchor.scope`: normal or build dependencies or resolved production graphs of published sc-runtime release crates? Judge subject overlap only.

criteria.no: The exclusion policy is unstated, is only a topic, or is violated. An unrelated dependency, dev-only fixture reference, or external help edit alone states no exclusion policy.
criteria.unclear: The text is ambiguous about the specific obligation; distinguish explicit omission from an indeterminate commitment.
criteria.yes: The text explicitly commits to production normal/build graphs excluding BOTH sc-compose and ATM workspace crates; equivalent copy/removal or external-only adapter architecture with this exclusion counts.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly commit to production release crates have no normal or build dependency on sc-compose or ATM agent-team-mail workspace crates, including agent-team-mail and atm-core? Judge the presence of this obligation only; silence is absence, not conflict. criteria.no: There is no explicit incompatible policy, including omission, unrelated work, or the scoped exception: dev-only test or benchmark references and external-executable invocation without a normal/build crate dependency.
criteria.unclear: A stated policy is ambiguous about whether it conflicts.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly adopt a policy incompatible with production release crates have no normal or build dependency on sc-compose or ATM agent-team-mail workspace crates, including agent-team-mail and atm-core? criteria.yes: The item's own deliverables implement, change or test the behavior the requirement is about.
criteria.no: The item only depends on, consumes, re-validates or defers this behavior, or works on something else.

criteria.yes: Reading only the item, a developer would know to deliver the requirement's condition and its specific result.

results.statement: In an app that has a SQLite database and enables cron, the default configuration MUST store cron rows in the app's SQLite database file.
results.quote: When an app has a SQLite database and enables cron, cron rows MUST by default be stored in that same SQLite database file.
results.context: Phase D planning session; option B storage decision
results.deterministic_check: generated SQLite+cron app: cron schedule table exists in the app database file and no other .db file is created under the instance root (test)

criteria.no: The item concerns a different subsystem (for example dependency bumps, advisories, transport, documentation of other features), or it expressly concerns only apps that have no SQLite database and leaves SQLite apps unchanged.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell whether it touches cron storage, cron wiring, or the SQLite store.
criteria.yes: The item changes, configures, or depends on cron storage, cron persistence configuration, the generated template's SQLite store, or cron wiring in an app that has a SQLite database.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` plan, change, or depend on how or where cron schedule rows are persisted, or the cron wiring, for an app that has a SQLite database? Signals: sc-cron's SQLite storage, a cron database location or URL setting, the generated template's SQLite store or database layout, or the template's cron wiring. Judge subject overlap only; do not judge whether the item obeys any rule.

criteria.no: The item is silent about where cron rows are stored, only mentions cron storage as a topic, or states a different default location such as a separate cron.db or schedules file.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions where cron rows go but it cannot be determined whether the default is the app's own SQLite database file.
criteria.yes: The item states that by default cron rows live in the app's SQLite database file, in any of the accepted wordings.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state that, by default, cron schedule rows are stored in the same SQLite database file as the app's own data? Accept equivalent wording: the cron table is created inside the app database (for example app.db), sc-cron reuses the app's SQLite pool, connection, or DATABASE_URL by default, or the app opens one database file holding both. An additional optional, non-default setting to move cron elsewhere does not remove a stated same-file default. Judge presence of this default only; do not judge conflict.

criteria.no: No stated default places cron rows outside the app's SQLite database file, including when the item is silent, only topical, compliant, offers only an opt-in override, or concerns apps without a SQLite database.
criteria.unclear: The item states a cron storage default whose location relative to the app's SQLite file cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: The item sets or keeps a default in which cron rows are stored outside the app's SQLite database file.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` make the default configuration store cron rows somewhere other than the app's SQLite database file in an app that has a SQLite database and enables cron? Examples of conflict: a separate cron.db or schedules.sqlite file by default, a separate cron database URL by default, or sharing the app file offered only as an opt-in. Not a conflict: silence about storage, topic-only mention, a same-file default, or an optional non-default override. Judge conflict only.

results.statement: Callers MUST NOT use spawn_blocking to submit writes to the SQLite writer.
results.quote: Every write to an app's SQLite database MUST go through one writer with an async channel input, a single thread that owns the only write connection, and batched transactions that reply after commit. No caller blocks or uses spawn_blocking to reach it.
results.context: Phase D planning session; option B storage decision
results.deterministic_check: grep: no spawn_blocking in callers of the SQLite writer

criteria.no: The item does not touch SQLite storage at all, for example README edits, CI, or file exports that do not involve the SQLite database.
criteria.unclear: The item's subject is too vague to place inside or outside the scope.
criteria.yes: The item implements or changes SQLite storage, SQLite store operations, the SQLite writer, or how callers submit writes to it.

relevant.instructions: Is `item.text` within `anchor.scope`: work that implements or changes a SQLite storage backend, the SQLite writer, or the generated template's SQLite store? An item that changes how handlers or tasks submit writes to the SQLite writer, its handle, channel, or batching is within scope even if it never mentions spawn_blocking. Using spawn_blocking for work unrelated to SQLite does not by itself put an item in scope. Judge scope only.

criteria.no: The item does not state how callers submit writes, states it without excluding spawn_blocking, or has some callers use spawn_blocking for submission.
criteria.unclear: The submission path is mentioned but whether it avoids spawn_blocking cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: The item states that callers submit SQLite writer writes without spawn_blocking.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` plan that writes to the SQLite writer are submitted without spawn_blocking, as `anchor.statement` requires? spawn_blocking used for reads, non-SQLite file I/O, or inside the writer's own thread is irrelevant to this question; look only at how callers submit writes to the SQLite writer. Judge presence only, not conflict.

criteria.no: The item states no such submission, whether it complies, is silent, or only uses spawn_blocking for unrelated work.
criteria.unclear: The item is ambiguous about whether some caller uses spawn_blocking to reach the writer.
criteria.yes: The item states such a spawn_blocking submission for at least one caller.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` propose doing something that `anchor.statement` rules out? For this anchor that means any caller, such as a handler, service, or scheduler, reaching the SQLite writer through spawn_blocking (for example spawn_blocking around blocking_send or around a synchronous submit method). Silence about how writes are submitted is not a contradiction. Judge conflict only.

criteria.unclear: Some text may state the requirement, but it is not possible to tell whether it states this specific content.

paraphrase.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one requirement (`anchor.statement`, area in `anchor.scope`). Does `item.text` contain a passage that means the same thing as `anchor.statement` but uses different words, numbers or structure (for example a count instead of a list, a synonym, or a summary phrase that a domain reader would take as equivalent)? Judge equivalence of meaning, not wording.

criteria.yes: A passage in the item means the same as the requirement in different words.
criteria.no: No passage in the item means the same as the requirement.
criteria.unclear: A passage is close in meaning but it is not possible to tell whether a domain reader would take it as equivalent.

partial.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one requirement (`anchor.statement`, area in `anchor.scope`). Split `anchor.statement` into its specific parts: the condition (mode, command, input or artifact) and each required result (behavior, error, value, count or prohibition). Does `item.text` state at least one of these parts but omit or blur at least one other? Judge completeness only.

criteria.yes: The item states some parts of the requirement and omits or blurs at least one other part.
criteria.no: The item states every part, or states none of them.
criteria.unclear: It is not possible to tell which parts the item covers.
